title: Drug gone. Do resistant cells go too?
hook: Resistance slows these bacteria down. Stop the drug: how fast does resistance fade?

knows: resistant bacteria survive a drug that kills the others
doesNotKnow: that resistance can carry a growth cost when the drug is absent
that a small cost removes resistance only slowly, so it lingers

misconception: Once the drug is gone, resistant bacteria quickly vanish.
objective: The learner can explain that in the toy dish a 5% growth cost takes resistant cells from 10% to only about 4% in 20 generations and 0.5% in 60: the cost shrinks their ratio to normal cells by 5% a generation, so resistance fades slowly and lingers.

claims.text: In the toy dish with no drug, if 10% of cells are resistant and they leave 5% fewer offspring each generation, the resistant share is 3.8% after 20 generations and 0.51% after 60.
claims.source: r_g = 0.1 x 0.95^g / (0.9 + 0.1 x 0.95^g): g = 20 gives 0.0383, g = 60 gives 0.0051 (Demo.tsx share(); node). Matches the brief's check (3.8%).

claims.text: A 5% cost shrinks the ratio of resistant to normal cells by 5% each generation, so the resistant share falls slowly and never reaches exactly zero.
claims.source: Ratio r/(1-r) multiplies by (1 - cost) per generation in the same model.

claims.text: Resistance often carries a fitness cost, and bacteria often gain extra (compensating) mutations that reduce that cost, so resistance can persist without the drug.
claims.source: Andersson & Hughes 2010, Nature Reviews Microbiology 8:260 ('Antibiotic resistance and its cost: is it possible to reverse resistance?').

claims.text: The dish is a model: a fixed 5% cost, no drug, no new mutations, no compensation, no randomness. It is a model, not treatment advice; stated on the stage ('Toy dish, no drug') and in the reveal.
claims.source: Model choice in Demo.tsx; brief life #39 (the 5% cost is invented). The stage also offers 1% and 10% costs (8.3% and 1.3% at generation 20).

recall.question: Resistant bacteria grow a little slower than normal ones when no drug is present. After the drug is stopped, the resistant share:
options: Drops to zero within a few generations
Shrinks slowly and can linger for a long time
recall.why: A small cost trims their share a little each generation, so it fades slowly; compensating mutations can slow it further.
